content: Amlexanox is a medication prescribed to treat mouth ulcers, specifically aphthous ulcers or canker sores. It works by reducing the time it takes for these ulcers to heal, which in turn alleviates the associated pain. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor, dentist, or pharmacist. Amlexanox is available as a beige-colored paste. It should be applied as soon as symptoms of an ulcer are noticed. Typically, it is used four times a day—after brushing and flossing your teeth following breakfast, lunch, dinner, and before bedtime. To apply, squeeze a quarter-inch of the paste onto your finger and gently dab it onto each ulcer in your mouth. Wash your hands immediately after application. This medication is intended for use only until the ulcer has healed, which usually occurs within 10 days. If significant healing has not occurred within this time frame, contact your physician or dentist. Always follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your healthcare provider if you have any questions. Use amlexanox exactly as directed, and do not use more or less of it or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Before using amlexanox, inform your doctor, dentist, or pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins and herbal supplements. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor or dentist. If you become pregnant while using amlexanox, contact your healthcare provider immediately. If you forget to apply a dose, do so as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Amlexanox may cause side effects. Minor side effects include slight pain, stinging, or burning of the skin that comes and goes, as well as nausea or diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor or dentist. A severe side effect, such as a rash, requires immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor or dentist while using this medication. Amlexanox is for external use only and should not come into contact with your eyes. If it does, rinse your eyes promptly. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. Notify your doctor or dentist if your ulcers worsen or do not improve within 10 days.
